correctness.rationale: The repaired claim is exactly the triangle variance correction, its all-size sign and its limit. Given the old graph, a distinct unordered target pair has probability 2/t² and contributes the multiplicity of its old edge. The old-edge sums of multiplicities and squared multiplicities are 2(t−1) and 2(t−1)+2D_t respectively, so the first conditional moment is deterministic and centered increments are orthogonal, while the second is 4(t−1)/t²+4D_t/t². E D_t=H_{t−1}; summing variances yields the formula with index cutoff n−1. The log-squared integral gives the Euler sum, with nonnegative terms allowing termwise integration; the other sums converge absolutely. The summand is 4f(t)/t², f(2)=0. Exact arithmetic checks f(3) through f(7) and f(21) negative and f(22) positive; the displayed first difference of f is positive from t=7 on. The correction first decreases strictly and then increases towards a strictly negative limit, with its rational upper bound below −1/5. This proves both zero cases n=2,3 and all negative cases n≥4. No inference about moments is made from total variation.

The exact n=6 mean and variance are 2951/900 and 2409749/810000; all tested entries, the finite rational sign anchors and the upper bound −0.20284246472146292 (rounded display of an exact rational) match. The bundled checker was inspected, not executed.

originality.rationale: The repaired final finding claims neither the mean, the parallel-pair variance, nor the cross-covariance. The checked same-model published statements give the known mean, distributional approximations, variance orders and overlap bounds, and a prior catalogue record gives the other matrix entries. None of those states or implies the exact triangle diagonal correction from their stated conclusions. The deterministic new-triangle mean and dependence of its conditional second moment on old double pairs supply the additional calculation.
residual_risks: A differently indexed calculation of exact triangle second moments in the same with-replacement model could predate the surviving claim.

value.rationale: The model's simplest nontrivial triangle statistic has a growing Poisson approximation, yet a fixed negative discrepancy in variance that is already strict at every size with a nonzero discrepancy. The exact all-size diagonal correction and limit are the missing information after the known cross-covariance. They constrain any moment-sensitive refinement of the same model and constitute more than an isolated size or a recasting of earlier bounds.
